neighbours.label: A place or people being measured against the rest of the world: the pole fires where a world-wide scope is in play or about to be stated ('Earth is⟦ the⟧ only planet…', 'a survey of 215 major⟦ cities⟧ of the world', 'one of the biggest⟦ in⟧ the world', nationals who must⟦ compete⟧ with foreigners). Local superlatives (the oldest church in the village) stay quiet.
fire: So far as anyone knows, Earth is the only planet where life has taken hold.
Vancouver came fourth in a study comparing 140 major cities around the globe.
The income gap in the country is one of the widest in the world.
If Kenyan growers are going to compete with producers from richer nations, they will need better roads.
As far as astronomers can tell, Earth is the only planet with open water on its surface.
Lagos is one of the fastest growing cities of Africa and the world.
The canal is among the busiest shipping lanes on the planet.
Melbourne placed near the top in a ranking of 170 large cities of the world.
quiet: So far as anyone knows, my grandmother is the only person who liked that soup.
Our team came fourth in a quiz against the other pubs on the street.
The gap between the two fences is one of the widest in the yard.
If the younger children are going to play with the older ones, they will need helmets.
As far as the teachers can tell, Emma is the only pupil who read the whole book.
The corner shop is one of the oldest buildings in the village.
The lane behind the mill is among the quietest paths in the parish.
My cousin placed near the top in a spelling contest at her school.

notes: Card: no single token (' on', ' in', ' of', ' the', ' cities', ' compete'); output promotes ' abroad', ' internationally', ' foreign', ' overseas', nationality adjectives.
